name: Medhu Vada
ingredients: 2 cups whole skinless urad dal (black gram)
instructions: 1. Soak urad dal for 2 to 3 hours, then drain and grind into a very thick, smooth batter using minimal water.
2. Whisk the batter vigorously for several minutes to incorporate air, ensuring it becomes light and fluffy.
3. Add finely chopped green chilies, ginger, curry leaves, crushed peppercorns, cilantro, asafoetida, and salt to the batter and mix well.
4. Heat oil in a deep pan for frying.
5. Wet your palms, take a portion of the batter, shape it into a round disc, and use your thumb to make a hole in the center.
6. Carefully slide the vada into the hot oil and fry on medium heat until golden brown and crispy on both sides.
7. Remove and drain on paper towels; serve hot with coconut chutney and sambar.
description: Medhu Vada is a quintessential South Indian breakfast staple often served during festivals, temple offerings, and daily meals. Known for its distinct donut shape and soft, airy texture, it is a hallmark of Tamil Brahmin and street food culture, typically paired with tangy coconut chutney or spicy sambar.
